reason: Added two independent off-the-reported-path levers: a stored-report worker that executes a stored definition on its own DuckDB connection outside the shared pool, and an alert diagnostics helper that performs a Go-level HTTP fetch to a caller-supplied webhook_url.

levers.shape: a stored report definition (stored by one request) is executed later on a fresh in-memory DuckDB opened with sql.Open outside configureDatabase, so the shared-pool sandbox and per-handler validation never see it
levers.skip_reason: looks like an admin-only background reporting helper built the way the compaction subprocess already opens its own DuckDB; it is not the reported query route, and it is a second copy of the separate-handle pattern reached through stored SQL
levers.coupled: functional/test_legit_flows.py::test_stored_report_returns_rows - a legitimate per-host aggregate report still runs and returns its rows, so refusing all reports is not a fix
levers.fairness: "No request may make the server open, read, list, return ... any local file outside its managed storage area ... This holds for every request, every caller-supplied value ... and every connection the server uses to run work."

levers.shape: the alert diagnostics endpoint POSTs to a caller-supplied webhook_url with Go's net/http; the address arrives in the request body, not in SQL, so it is a second implementation of caller-driven egress that no database-level protection can reach
levers.skip_reason: an operator diagnostics helper for an external notification system: it is neither the reported query route nor a SQL sink, so a database sandbox, a SQL validator and a route audit centred on the query API all miss it
levers.coupled: functional/test_legit_flows.py::test_alert_delivery_uses_configured_receiver - delivery to the operator-configured receiver still works, so removing outbound delivery is not a fix
levers.fairness: "No request may make the server contact a network address supplied by the caller ... every caller-supplied value ... Nothing a caller sends may disable or relax this protection"; the refusal rule also requires an attempt to be an error response.

fail_confidence_reason: Two independent mechanism-level levers sit off the reported path (stored SQL on a connection of its own, and Go-level caller-chosen egress) with coupled must-keep-working values on both sides, but a thorough route-by-route audit plus the coupled flows could still close both within three runs.
